expectations.name: ranked-multi-archetype-proposals
expected_behavior: Opens with the resolved library, the consumer scope, and the call-site count
Proposes across several archetypes, including at least one structural move — absorbing the repeated sequence, or moving a responsibility upstream — not only a rename or a single helper
Ranks by net impact and shows the working: each row's Reach is a fraction of the stated N, and the one-line rationale names what it trades against

Every proposal shows a before → after taken from one real call site, cited `file:line` and matching that file's text there — no composite excerpt spanning files, no placeholder where the before belongs
Offers concrete diffs, since the library source is editable here

expectations.name: proposals-stay-on-the-library
expected_behavior: Every proposal changes `oskit`'s API; the consumer diff is shown as the payoff, never as the proposal itself
Names the call-site-only cleanup it declined and why, rather than silently omitting it — the reader needs to see the trap was spotted
Proposed signatures follow the style Naming, Errors, and API design rules
Edits nothing — reports the proposal set and stops

expectations.name: external-library-public-surface
expected_behavior: Detects that the library is external and says so
Frames every proposal at the public-API level and notes it cannot diff internals
Offers a local wrapper as the fallback for changes that cannot land upstream

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: No narration: the reply opens on the headline line and the table. A one-line note that call sites were mapped by grep rather than a language server is a fact, not narration
Says in one line that the forced structural option was considered and what displaced it, if the cap evicted it — the cap hides nothing silently
States each proposal once, with no closing summary re-listing the table already shown

expectations.name: restraint-on-an-api-that-is-fine
expected_behavior: Says the API fits its consumer and prints no ranked table, rather than an empty one
Names what it looked for and found absent, so a reader can tell a clean API from a shallow pass
Declines any reach-1 shape by name instead of padding the table with a `Low` row
Still reports the header line with the real call-site count
